Are two co founders are David and Tony.
So David spent 25 years in venture capital and he raised over $165 million invested in 50 different companies and five of those wound up going public and selling for over 165 million each.
And Tony was a VP at a multi billion dollar IT company here in Dallas.
So as you can see, very technology related.
And so yeah, in terms of why we like the company, we are doing a roll up of marketing consulting, digital marketing type firms and we're looking for companies that have.
Have an edge that I guess differentiate themselves.

And this company when we saw it seemed like it had a very, I don't know, like a very good differentiator with the experiential side and a lot of high profile clients and I mean yeah, we really liked what we saw.

A lot of fun, a lot of good times.
And it just the through line was, you know, great visual storytelling.
That was kind of everything I did, whether it was long form, short form, big name artists, smaller artists.
And when I relocated out of the city to Connecticut, I worked for my one and only ad agency.
It was an omnicom agency here and I ran their broadcast.
I was in charge of all their commercials.

It was just really a culture clash for me in that agency.
Just seeing how steeped agencies still were in excessive layers and you know, prolonged timelines and sort of, you know, not treating their clients very well.
So, you know, of course that agency went on the downswing and at that point I was a single mom and knew I needed to kind of grab the reins of my own future.

And I started Imaginary Content thinking actually our sweet spot would be as an external resource for a lot of other agencies in this area, our significant agencies, but they don't have internal video or content production arms.
So I thought we would be kind of a resource for them.
And we were.
Initially we did 300 videos for Facebook, we did over 100 videos for eBay through other agencies in the beginning.

And you know, here we are nine years later as recognized best in class industry leaders in that world.
Where our right to win category is the content.

You see, if you're buying a product on Amazon or Target or Walmart, you know, all of that SEO geo optimized copy we do internally, we create all the images, we create the strategy behind those images, we do videos, all to support the e commerce conversion of consumers on the digital shelf.

Just absolute rock stars.
True, true creative talents.

We turned around in about three days.
Crazy, but super fun and you know, great for the socials and great for our clients to enjoy that.
We have that side of, of the company as well.
So that's just very, very top line.
You know, I don't have any partners, never had no investors.
It's a very clean company and you know, looking to see how we find the right path to, you know, continuing to, to grow the company.

I mean, yeah, it's an incredible story to hear that you were able to build all of that.
I just reckon we just had our third daughter, so I. Yeah, doing everything as a single mom, it's very impressive.
So.
But yeah, what's kind of your dream circumstance?
Like, are you looking to stay on?
Do you want to sell and you know, kind of be done?
Do you want to stay on for two to three years in a perfect scenario?
What would that look like for you?

Would that work for you?
And I'm like, oh, that could be interesting.
So I would say I'm open.
I.

I can tell you, like, that's easier to rule out.
Right.

summary.overview:
- **Market Position:** Imaginary Content leads in e-commerce content, focusing on SEO-optimized copy, images, and videos for platforms like Amazon.

- **Client Relationships:** Long-term partnerships, especially with Kraft Heinz since 2017, enhance stability and attractiveness for potential buyers.

- **Operational Structure:** The company has 21 employees, prioritizing in-house collaboration and creative quality, supported by a dedicated 6,000 sq ft office.

- **Acquisition Goals:** Baymark Partners seeks marketing firms with strong client ties, aiming for a $10 million EBITDA among their portfolio.

- **AI Usage:** AI tools support, but human creativity is essential; clients remain cautious about AI-generated marketing content.

- **Competitive Offers:** Multiple buyers, including Baymark, are engaged. LOI deadline end of February increases urgency for securing deals.
summary.short_summary: The meeting discussed Imaginary Content's unique niche in e-commerce content production, emphasizing its expertise in SEO-optimized product details and digital marketing. Founded and led by Ilene Richardson, the company maintains strong client relationships, particularly with long-time partner Kraft Heinz, and operates two divisions focusing on e-commerce and experiential projects. Baymark Partners presented their acquisition strategy, targeting marketing firms with strong revenue metrics and client retention. The team highlighted their growth strategy anchored in client referrals and the cautious approach to utilizing AI in content creation. With multiple prospective buyers in engagement and a looming Letter of Intent deadline, urgency for favorable offers was underscored.
